children: , the cloud and software powerhouse backing OpenAI, entered the summary-judgment phase of consolidated copyright litigation brought by authors and news organizations. Shares slipped approximately 0.4% to $492.22 Wednesday morning. The chart shows the stock trading 15.58% below its GF Value estimate of $583.09, suggesting the legal uncertainty may already be weighing on its valuation.

The Authors Guild wants the court to rule that Microsoft and OpenAI infringed copyrights and cannot rely on fair use. The defendants are pushing the opposite case through their own motions. Nothing has been decided yet. These are competing legal claims, and unresolved questions could still head to trial.

The stakes stretch far beyond one courtroom. Microsoft ended June with more than 30 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats and generated $59.3 billion in quarterly cloud revenue. A tougher copyright standard could force more licensing deals, tighter dataset controls and heavier documentation across future AI models. A defense victory would protect greater operating freedom, but appeals and other lawsuits would keep the issue alive.

title: Microsoft Slips as AI Copyright Fight Reaches Judgment Stage
